newsitem.title: DUBAI: SASREF TO EXPAND OIL REFINERY IN SAUDI ARABIA.
newsitem.headline: SASREF TO EXPAND OIL REFINERY IN SAUDI ARABIA.

text.p: Saudi Aramco Shell Refining Company (Sasref) has received bids from foreign contractors to expand and modify its Jubail oil refinery, the London-based Middle East Economic Digest (MEED) business weekly reported in its latest edition.

"The $140 million scheme calls for the installation of a new thermal gasoil unit/gas turbine (tgu/gt) designed to raise yield and improve efficiency at the Jubail refinery," MEED said in its August 8 publication.

The export-orientated Jubail joint venture refinery has a nominal capacity of 305,000 barrels per day (bpd), making it the second largest of the seven refineries on Saudi soil, according to oil industry estimates.
The grassroots scheme which would use Shell technology involves the integration of the gas turbine with the refinery's visbreaker.
A contract for the basic design and engineering is expected to be awared by the end of the year.
"Mechanical completion will be some 26-28 months later," MEED quoted industry sources as saying.
"The Sasref refinery has been operating at a cost deficit for many years and could be due for further upgrading in the future," MEED reported.
Sasref is a joint venture between state oil firm Saudi Aranoc and the Royal Dutch Shell Group.
